newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products mixed, mogas dips $1 with north.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products mixed, mogas dips $1 with north.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were mixed on Thursday, traders said.
Gasoline slipped $1 a tonne in line with northwest Europe but naphtha gained a similar amount.

Gas oil prices lost some ground on the back of weaker IPE gas oil futures but traders said the underlying trend was firmer with refinery run-cuts further limiting diesel supplies while recent East Med demand drew down 0.2 sulphur heating oil supplies.
Tighter avails of both grades maintained a narrow premium for diesel over heating oil leaving refiners reluctant to run the more expensive to make EN590 diesel.
Good buying pegged scarce prompt diesel cargo bids around $156 fob Med with one cargo offered around $2 higher. Demand for second half July was also seen staying strong.
Tighter 0.2 sulphur heating oil supplies were valued around $160 fob Italy.
High sulphur fuel oil was virtually unchanged with supplies said to be still tight for both cracked and straight-run material. Traders valued cargoes around $88 cif.

One percent was described as a very slow market with a major Italian buyer said to be relaxed, "looking for only for dribs and drabs here and there" after picking up a cargo in the north on Tuesday at $104 cif.
A NWE trader said that the Italian buyer could be a potential buyer of a cargo it picked up earlier this week in the north at $92.50 fob.
